# Known limitations in v5.1.1

This page describes the published v5.1.1 binary, not planned features. The
[GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/neverhuman/redline/issues) had no
open issues when checked on 2026-10-06. That does not mean the engine has no
known defects. The dated [issue snapshot](../scripts/docs/issues.json) is
retained with the documentation check. The parity policies, capability matrix
and durability contract
below record limitations separately from GitHub issues.

## What the compatibility evidence measures

The following block is generated from the committed official evidence and
its exclusion policies. Expected errors, declared refusals and skipped cases
do not establish support for a feature. The PostgreSQL lane compares
normalized SQL-shell transcripts; it is not a wire protocol or typed-result
certification.

Evidence source: `af4fc74cc3280582c4e6bd0583fe503c83118c48`; processed evidence SHA-256: `48c16188cb95ee836f30b139242a38cef428437d5ebe0d967db41e0ec4307c54`.

Known SQLite failures (also present in the memory lane):

- `00076` — EXPLAIN_BYTECODE: EXPLAIN prints RedlineDB's operator tree; the case declares the SQLite VDBE opcodes Init and ResultRow, and RedlineDB has no VDBE.
- `00133` — DOT_AUTH: `.auth on` installs no authorizer. RedlineDB's authorizer fires different events from SQLite's, so there is no SQLite-shaped `authorizer: SELECT NULL NULL NULL NULL` line to print; passing would take made-up output, so the case stays failing by decision (2026-09-29).
- `00140` — DOT_EXPERT_OPTIONAL: `.expert` has no index advisor: it prints a fixed recommendation written for one fixture, twice, without sqlite3's blank separator lines or the `(a=?)` constraint on the SEARCH line. Passing would take made-up output, so the case stays failing by decision (2026-09-29).
- `00209` — OPT_INTERACTIVE_CATALOG: The case compares sqlite3's own `-interactive` banner (`SQLite version 3.53.1 ...`) and prompts byte for byte. RedlineDB is not SQLite; its `-interactive` stub ignores stdin and prints `sqlite>` without the trailing space or the final newline. Matching would mean impersonating sqlite3's banner, so the case stays failing by decision (2026-09-29).
- `10229` — OPT_PCACHETRACE: `-pcachetrace` is accepted but prints nothing; the case declares the PCACHETRACE page-cache trace on stderr.

## Storage and recovery

- A database is a native-format directory. SQLite tools cannot open it; the
  SQLite-shaped help banner does not describe its storage format.
- Automatic keys are per table. They are not globally unique across tables.
  `AUTOINCREMENT` does not persist `sqlite_sequence` across a reopen, so a
  previously deleted high key can be reused. See the
  [upgrade note](upgrade-v5.1.1.md).
- The Strict process-kill receipt covers its recorded filesystem and
  workload. It does not certify OS crashes, power loss, corrupt media, or
  arbitrary checkpoint crash points. Killing a checkpoint before its
  control slot lands can leave a duplicate row visible to a page scan; the
  existing receipt forces no checkpoint. See the
  [durability contract](manual/durability.md#checkpoints-and-log-retention).
- One process must own a database directory. CLI read-only opens, sqlx
  `mode=ro`, SQL `ATTACH` and the C API have owner-lock exceptions described
  in [operation](manual/09-operate.md#one-writer-process-many-connections).
  Read-only does not make concurrent recovery safe.

## SQL and result shapes

- `fts5`, `rtree` and `dbstat` names provide ordinary-table stand-ins for
  selected corpus statements, not SQLite's modules. Module and compile-option
  listings are not proof that those features exist.
- `EXPLAIN` uses RedlineDB's operator tree, not SQLite VDBE bytecode.
  `.auth` does not install a SQLite authorizer, `.expert` has no real index
  adviser, `-interactive` is a banner/prompt stub, and `-pcachetrace` does not
  emit a page-cache trace.
- `ROLLBACK TO` replays deterministic statements before the savepoint and
  refuses replay-unsafe statements. A failed statement can end an explicit
  transaction. `INSTEAD OF UPDATE/DELETE` trigger definitions are accepted,
  but modifying the view fails; `INSERT ... SELECT` does not fire an
  `AFTER INSERT` trigger. See [transactions](manual/07-transactions.md).
- PostgreSQL predicate booleans can print `t`/`f`, while literal and stored
  boolean values can print `1`/`0`. Do not assume a single representation
  from the dialect variable alone.
- `::citext` case-insensitive comparison requires `CREATE EXTENSION citext`
  in the session first. A column declared `citext` is refused. Domain
  constraints are checked on explicit domain casts; a domain-typed table
  column does not enforce the same check on an ordinary inserted integer.
  Schema/type/extension state is session-scoped, so reconnecting does not
  recreate a PostgreSQL catalog.
- `NOTIFY`/`pg_notify`, WAL-position SQL functions and snapshot export are
  refused with `unsupported capability:`. Replication/publication catalog
  shims do not deliver events or replicate data. No PostgreSQL wire protocol,
  TLS, roles, SQLSTATE or cross-process advisory-lock guarantee is provided.
  See the [capability matrix](beyond-postgres-skips.md#capability-matrix).
- `Engine::begin(Serializable)` in the Rust API is refused. SQL accepts
  `SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE` as a session label; that
  label does not establish serializable storage isolation. A fresh
  `BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE` is accepted while `SHOW
  transaction_isolation` still reports `read committed`. RQL covers the
  phase-1 relational surface rather than the whole SQL language.

```sql doctest postgres
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE;
SHOW transaction_isolation;
-- prints: serializable
```

```sql doctest postgres
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE;
SHOW transaction_isolation;
ROLLBACK;
-- prints: read committed
```

The boolean distinction is executable documentation:

```sql doctest postgres
SELECT true, false;
SELECT 1 = 1, 1 = 2;
-- prints: 1|0
-- prints: t|f
```

SQLite `STRICT` tables reject `BOOLEAN` and `UUID` column types. The optional
Rust PostgreSQL reference lane contains a conflicting strict-storage
expectation; its failure before insertion is not a measured PostgreSQL
storage match. See [reference-lane scope](testing.md).

```sql doctest error
CREATE TABLE typed(flag BOOLEAN) STRICT;
-- error: unknown datatype for typed.flag: "BOOLEAN"
```

```sql doctest error
CREATE TABLE typed(ident UUID) STRICT;
-- error: unknown datatype for typed.ident: "UUID"
```

## Interrupts and runtime bounds

The Rust `InterruptHandle` sets a flag shared by connections to the same
live database. It is checked at API entry and before statement steps, not
inside an already-running executor step. The flag remains set; opening
another connection to that live database does not clear it. Busy timeouts
cover lock waits, not arbitrary query execution. Use an application-owned
worker process and external timeout when execution must have a deadline.
See the [executable interrupt example](manual/03-for-agents.md).

## CLI and C API

The CLI accepts some SQLite-shaped options without implementing the named
SQLite facility. `-heap N MIN` in help is inaccurate: only one heap argument
is parsed. `-vfs`, `-mmap`, `-lookaside`, heap and encoding options do not
configure SQLite subsystems. `-nofollow` checks path existence but follows
an existing symlink. These flags are not memory limits or path-security
controls. See [CLI reference](cli.md).

The C ABI is an experimental subset. A symbol being present does not mean
every flag or hook has SQLite semantics. In particular, the authorizer is
not called for `SQLITE_READ`, DDL and several other operations; trace-v2
events and the busy-handler callback are not implemented. Review
[security capabilities](security-capabilities.md) before relying on a hook
for access control. A release panic aborts the process, including through
the C API.

## Performance scope

The [README engine table](../README.md#engine-throughput) is generated from
the publishable paired-rerun21 bundle. Normal numbers measure tmpfs,
single-process work; Strict has its own real-disk paired controls. Workload,
fixture and durability mode define each comparison. The separate CLI
history table includes process startup and ends at v5.0.0. Historical and
unverified numbers in [performance history](performance-history.md) are
not new measurements for v5.1.1.
